body.statement: Under \(D_L^{\mathrm G}\), \(\mathbb E[X_s^{\infty}]=0\), \(\mathbb E[X_s^{\infty}X_t^{\infty}]=\mathbf 1\{s=t\}\), and \(\mathbb E[X_{t_1}^{\infty}X_{t_2}^{\infty}X_{t_3}^{\infty}X_{t_4}^{\infty}]=\Theta_L(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4)\) for all integer indices. Every affine Boolean block \(W\) satisfies \(|C_{L,h}(W)|\le h\) for \(1\le h\le d<L/2\), so \(\operatorname{tr}(M_L+H_d)\le\sum_{h=1}^{d}(h^2+h)\). Moreover, \(T^{-1}\mathbb E[C_T(X^{\infty})C_T(X^{\infty})^{\top}]\to(M_L+H_d)/L\). Equivalently, \(B\) complete blocks have lag-sum covariance \(B M_L+(B-1)H_d\), and all covariances between internal and boundary lag sums vanish.
body.justification: This is the coefficient-level fourth-moment and endpoint certificate needed to transfer a classical code into a one-path causal randomization law.
body.gap: Golay and Davis--Jedwab prove complementary autocorrelation identities, and Mazáč proves infinite Rudin--Shapiro correlation recurrences; none supplies this independent-block random-phase tensor and boundary covariance.
body.consumer: The certificate makes the design auditable and yields exact risk for the actual zero-prehistory moment estimator rather than a circular surrogate.
body.proof_tex:
First consider one block in \(\texttt{def:golay-block-law}\).  For a multiset \(J=(j_1,\ldots,j_m)\), direct multiplication gives
\[
\prod_{r=1}^{m}W_{j_r}
=\sigma^m(-1)^{\sum_{r=1}^{m}\phi_L(j_r)}
 (-1)^{\alpha\cdot(\bigoplus_{r=1}^{m}j_r)}.
\tag{4}
\]
The average over the fair sign \(\sigma\) is zero when \(m\) is odd.  When \(m\) is even, orthogonality of the characters of \(\mathbb F_2^p\) gives
\[
2^{-p}\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb F_2^p}(-1)^{\alpha\cdot h}
=\mathbf1\{h=0\}.
\]
Applying this identity to (4) proves exactly the coefficient \(\kappa_L(J)\) in \(\texttt{def:fourth-tensor-certificate}\).

Condition on the uniform block phase.  Indices in different blocks involve independent block parameters, so their joint moment factors over blocks; within each block the factor is the just-computed \(\kappa_L\).  Averaging over the \(L\) phases proves
\[
\mathbb E[X_{t_1}^{\infty}X_{t_2}^{\infty}X_{t_3}^{\infty}X_{t_4}^{\infty}]
=\Theta_L(t_1,t_2,t_3,t_4).
\]
The same calculation with one index gives mean zero.  With two distinct indices, either they lie in different blocks and centeredness applies, or they lie in one block and their binary labels have nonzero xor, so the character average is zero.  Since every square is one,
\[
\mathbb E[X_s^{\infty}X_t^{\infty}]=\mathbf1\{s=t\}.
\]

We next establish the autocorrelation bound without importing it as a hypothesis.  Suppress the irrelevant global sign.  For a length \(2^r\) affine word \(P_r\), define \(Q_r(j)=(-1)^{j_{r-1}}P_r(j)\).  Splitting on the highest bit gives, for a sign \(\varepsilon\) determined by the corresponding affine coefficient,
\[
P_r=(P_{r-1},\varepsilon Q_{r-1}),
\qquad Q_r=(P_{r-1},-\varepsilon Q_{r-1}).
\tag{5}
\]
At length two the aperiodic autocorrelations of \(P_1\) and \(Q_1\) cancel.  If the two words at level \(r-1\) have cancelling autocorrelations at every positive lag, then (5) shows the same at level \(r\): below the half-length the two within-half sums add to twice the preceding complementary sum while the two crossing sums cancel, and at or above the half-length only the crossing sums remain and cancel.  Induction therefore proves
\[
C_{P_r,h}+C_{Q_r,h}=0\qquad(1\leq h<2^r).
\tag{6}
\]
For the single length-\(L\) word \(W=(P_{p-1},\varepsilon Q_{p-1})\), a shift \(h<L/2\) has two within-half contributions, which cancel by (6), and exactly \(h\) crossing products.  Hence \(|C_{L,h}(W)|\leq h\).  At \(h=L/2\) there are only \(h\) crossing products, so the same bound holds there as well.  In particular, it applies for every \(1\leq h\leq d\) whenever \(L\geq2d\), and the displayed strict-range assertion follows.

Because \(M_L\) is the second moment matrix of the lag-sum vector,
\[
\operatorname{tr}(M_L+H_d)
=\sum_{h=1}^{d}\bigl(\mathbb E[C_{L,h}(W)^2]+h\bigr)
\leq\sum_{h=1}^{d}(h^2+h).
\tag{7}
\]

For the covariance limit, first align a window with \(B\) complete blocks.  Let \(I_b=C_L(W^{(b)})\), and for the boundary from block \(b\) to block \(b+1\) put
\[
J_{b,h}=\sum_{i=0}^{h-1}W^{(b)}_{L-h+i}W^{(b+1)}_i,
\qquad 1\leq h\leq d.
\]
Pairwise orthogonality within a block gives \(\mathbb E[I_b]=0\) and
\[
\mathbb E[J_{b,h}J_{b,k}]
=\sum_{i=0}^{h-1}\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}
 \mathbb E[W^{(b)}_{L-h+i}W^{(b)}_{L-k+j}]
 \mathbb E[W^{(b+1)}_iW^{(b+1)}_j]
=h\mathbf1\{h=k\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus \(\mathbb E[J_bJ_b^{\top}]=H_d\).  Different internal vectors are independent.  An internal--boundary product contains a single centered factor from the other block, and a product of boundary vectors at different boundaries contains a single centered factor from an outer block (unless the boundaries coincide).  Hence all such cross-covariances vanish.  The exact aligned identity is consequently
\[
\mathbb E[C_{BL}(X^{\infty})C_{BL}(X^{\infty})^{\top}]
=BM_L+(B-1)H_d.
\tag{9}
\]
A general random-phase window differs from an aligned union of complete blocks by at most two partial blocks and a fixed number, depending only on \(L,d\), of crossing products.  Its remainder is deterministically bounded for fixed \(L,d\); (9) and Cauchy--Schwarz show that its covariance contribution divided by \(T\) vanishes.  Since \(B/T\to1/L\),
\[
T^{-1}\mathbb E[C_T(X^{\infty})C_T(X^{\infty})^{\top}]
\longrightarrow\frac{M_L+H_d}{L}.
\]

For the requested finite checks, direct substitution of all affine masks at both \(L=8\) and \(L=16\) gives the four values
\[
(C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4)\in
\{(-1,0,-1,0),\,(-1,0,3,0),\,(1,0,-3,0),\,(1,0,1,0)\}
\]
with equal multiplicities (respectively two and four masks, before the duplicate global signs).  Hence, for both lengths,
\[
M_L\big|_{d=3}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1\\0&0&0\\-1&0&5\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
(M_L+H_3)=\begin{pmatrix}2&0&-1\\0&2&0\\-1&0&8\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For \(d=2\) the leading blocks are \(M_L=\operatorname{Diag}(1,0)\) and \(M_L+H_2=2I_2\).  These enumerations agree with (7)--(9) and verify the endpoint normalization for \(K=3,4\).
